evidence.title: Improved research execution does not ensure expert acceptance of research results
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: CRUX reports that both follow-up research papers were rejected by expert reviewers, despite improvements in experimental design and resource management. The two trials are separate task outcomes within one evaluation programme. Observation period and measurement context: Initial work early July 2026; follow-up trials September 2026.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded account; study or measurement; not independently reproduced
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative or qualifying; does not validate a definition

source_locations.SRC-125: Original reports: setup, expert reviews, limitations and appendices

evidence.limitations: Two tasks; non-blind review by original authors; changed scaffolds and one manual reset. Improvements were real within these tests. Follow-up papers and full logs were unpublished. This does not establish that AI cannot do research.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer to other populations, tasks and operating environments remains unestablished. Missing measurement details are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: Research execution and research judgment are distinct assurance questions.
evidence.dispute_status: See source version and dispute qualifications; no systematic clearance claimed.
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Successor assurance
terms.definition: Evaluation of whether a significantly modified or AI-created successor preserves specified behavioral, authorization, evidence, control, and purpose-related properties. Passing performance tests alone does not demonstrate preservation of these properties.

relationships.explanation: Qualifies extrapolation from successful engineering execution to autonomous research judgment.
